notes.source: Predibase LoRA Land adapters (same recipe: Mistral-7B-v0.1, r=8, alpha=16, q_proj+v_proj), safetensors only; base tensors read with HTTP range requests (o_proj of 3 layers per adapter, lm_head, final norm). CPU, no forward pass.
notes.where: every adapter puts most of its energy in the last third of the layers (q 41-65%, v 50-75%); peak layer 28-31 for 6 of 8; jigsaw (toxicity) peaks earlier (q L23, v L13).
notes.how_many: mean effective rank 1.4-3.0 out of 8: each task uses 2-3 directions per matrix.
notes.logit_lens: task-readable poles on some strong v_proj layers: jigsaw L30 yes/no/NO (its label words), conllpp L28 opening quotes and brackets (structured output), cnn L30 NEW/Updated/The (news headline), customer_support L29 order/page/profile vs box/names. gsm8k, magicoder, glue_sst2 and legal show mostly junk tokens: their write is not a readable token push. The sign of an SVD direction is arbitrary without activations.
notes.overlap_artifact: input-side subspace overlap is 0.80 (chance 0.002), but the raw A matrices of different adapters have element-wise cosine 0.57-0.84 and the top input direction is spread over all coordinates (top-5 coords 1.3%): the adapters share the random init seed of A, so the input overlap is the init, not learning. A drifts most in late layers (cos 0.84 at L5 vs 0.66 at L30). Output side (B, learned from zero): overlap 0.013-0.028, about 7-14x chance: different tasks write different directions.
notes.lesson: comparing LoRAs by their A matrices is invalid when they share an init seed; compare B (or B A) and check raw A cosine first.
